findings.message: `trap '_monitor_interrupt_handler' TERM INT` clobbers whatever TERM/INT handler the calling process already had installed (e.g. the runner's established re-arm handler per #1759/#1860) without saving it first, and `trap - TERM INT` on line 191 resets the disposition to default rather than restoring the prior handler — so if plugin.sh's functions are sourced into the runner's own process (as the dispatch convention comment implies), any SIGTERM/SIGINT delivered after this window (during subsequent report-writing, cleanup hooks, or later stages sharing the process) now gets the OS default action instead of whatever graceful handling existed before, silently weakening the engine's shutdown/cleanup guarantees for the remainder of the process lifetime.

deploy_result_json/pr_url_txt paths are taken verbatim from ZBUILD_STAGE_INPUTS and dereferenced (`-f` test, `jq -c .`, file read) with no check that the resolved path stays within the expected state/artifacts directory; their content is then folded into the model prompt with only route_to_model's generic redaction as a backstop, so any path an upstream/engine component places in that index gets read off disk and sent to the external model.

`_mon_out_ref` and `_mon_interrupted` are assigned without `local`, so they leak into the enclosing shell/global namespace; harmless under the current single-invocation-per-process dispatch model but a latent footgun if monitor_stage_run is ever invoked more than once in the same sourced shell (e.g. retried in-process, or reused by a future harness change), since a signal racing the very first assignment on a later call would still see the previous run's stale `_mon_out_ref`.
